lines.text: What if you could never die?
No ageing, no illness. You stay exactly as you are, forever.
Eighty years later. The average person lives about seventy three years,
so almost everyone you grew up with is gone.
Five hundred years. Language has changed so much you can barely follow a conversation.
Your quiet town is now a giant city.
Ten thousand years. That's twice as long as all of written history.
Today's cities are buried ruins, and you may be the only one who remembers them.
One million years. Humans might have changed beyond recognition, or left for other worlds.
The river has carved a whole new valley.
Two hundred and fifty million years. The continents crash together into a new supercontinent, and volcanoes erupt across a scorching land.
One billion years. The Sun has grown so bright that the oceans start to evaporate.

segments.caption: Still here
segments.fact: THE SUN BECOMES A RED GIANT

lines.text: Five billion years. The Sun swells into a red giant, filling the sky. And you are still here.
So, would you still want to live forever?
